text:
Predicates:
DeadlyDisease(x) ::: x is a deadly disease.
LowSurvivalRate(x) ::: x comes with a low survival rate.
SevereCancer(x) ::: x is a severe cancer.
BileDuctCancer(x) ::: x is bile duct cancer.
Cancer(x) ::: x is cancer.
AllCancer(x) ::: x is all cancer.
Cholangiocarcinoma(x) ::: x is Cholangiocarcinoma.
MildFlu(x) ::: x is mild flu.
ColorectalCancer(x) ::: x is colorectal cancer.
WithLowSurvival(x) ::: x has low survival rate.
Both(x, y) ::: x is both y.

Premises:
∀x (DeadlyDisease(x) → LowSurvivalRate(x)) ::: If something is a deadly disease, then it comes with a low survival rate.
SevereCancer(cancer) ::: Severe cancers are deadly diseases.
SevereCancer(bileDuctCancer) ::: Bile duct cancer is a severe cancer.
AllCancer(Cholangiocarcinoma) ::: All Cholangiocarcinoma is bile duct cancer.
AllCancer(BileDuctCancer) ::: All bile duct cancer is a cancer.
AllCancer(ColorectalCancer) ::: All colorectal cancer is a cancer.
MildFlu comes with a low survival rate ::: Mild flu comes with a low survival rate.
¬Both(ColorectalCancer, BileDuctCancer) ∧ ¬Both(ColorectalCancer, LowSurvivalRate) ::: Colorectal cancer is not both a bile duct cancer and with a low survival rate.

Conclusion:
Uncertain ::: Colorectal cancer is a kind of severe cancer.
